prompt: You are the test author: write the checks that separate a correct distinct-word counter from one that minds capitals, one that splits on a single space, and one that dies on null.
explanation: Every broken scanner here is right about a tidy sentence of single-spaced lowercase words, which is exactly why a happy-path test proves nothing. Each bug has its own revealing input: mixed capitals expose the case-sensitive count, a doubled space exposes split(" ") producing an empty token, and only null exposes the missing guard. Wrapping the calls in try/catch and returning false turns a crash into an ordinary failed check instead of an exception escaping the checker.
hints: Start with "the cat The CAT sat" -> 3. A scanner that treats The and the as different words answers 5.
Add an input with two spaces in a row, such as "one  two" -> 2 -- split(" ") produces an empty token there and counts 3.
Put every call in one try block ending with catch (Throwable t) { return false; }, and remember to pass null and "" as sentences.
